newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Second Chance plans department store after IPO.
newsitem.headline: Second Chance plans department store after IPO.

text.p: Second Chance Enterprises Ltd (SCE), the soon-to-be-listed Singapore gold and fashion retailer, said on Thursday it would consolidate its retail outlets into one department store within two years.
"If our plans for a department store are a success, all our shops catering for Malay clients (in Singapore) will be replaced by it," managing director Mohamed Salleh told a news conference.
He said the new department store floor area could be five times the 7,700 sq ft currently housed in seven outlets.
No site has been found for the store. Rental and freehold options were being considered, Salleh said.
Launching an initial public offering (IPO) of a total of 19 million shares in SCE to raise Singapore $5.25 million, Salleh said he saw new SCE outlets opening in the region in the next five years.
SCE has one jewellery store in Malaysia and could move into Indonesia, Salleh said.

Salleh said a niche approach meant SCE avoided the retail downturn, achieving average annual compound growth of 44.9 percent compared to a 1.7 percent decline in the retail sales index for textile and personal effects, between 1992 and 1996.
DBS Investment Research Pte Ltd, a unit of DBS Bank and the IPO manager, underwriter and agent, said it expected net profit growth to be about 12 percent per annum in 1997, 1998 and 1999.
Pre-tax profit in 1996 was S$4.56 million from S$0.13 million in 1992.
Salleh said the launch of the company on the stock market was significant as it would be the first Malay-owned and run company to be listed in Singapore.
Salleh said SCE's mission to "totally dominate the Malay market and to have a finger in every Malay pie" could see it exploit other product areas beyond jewellery and fashion.
He said the department store plan included space for a halal supermarket and foodcourt and SCE's niche approach would see it open its first Chinese-targeted jewellery store this year.
